logic.note: Off below the ~1 V threshold, on above it; the body diode conducts S → D when the drain is pulled below the source.

timing.note: Switches with each re-solve: no gate charge, no switching losses, PWM edges are ideal.

analog.note: Rds(on) steps with Vgs (5 Ω at 1.0-1.5 V, 0.1 Ω to 2.5 V, 0.04 Ω to 4.5 V, 0.028 Ω above), from the datasheet's typical curves; the linear (saturation) region is not modelled, so a half-on gate looks like a small resistor, not a current limit.

power.note: Reports I²R heating above 1.4 W (SOT-23 on a small board) and over-current; the part does not fail.

emulates: Logic-level switching from a 3.3 V GPIO
Floating-gate, gate over-voltage and heating diagnostics
doesNotEmulate: Gate charge, switching speed and losses at high PWM frequency
testOnRealDevice: How warm it gets at your load current
PWM above a few kHz: the gate needs a stronger driver
